question: Your CI pipeline uses Claude Code to review pull requests. To cut noisy comments, the team added the line "Only report high-confidence findings" to the review prompt. Two weeks later, the number of review comments has dropped by about 40%. However, developers still dismiss the same share of the remaining comments as style nitpicks, and a few real null-pointer bugs that earlier reviews caught are now missing. What should the team do next?

options.text: Strengthen the line so that Claude reports a finding only when it is nearly certain, which should push the remaining style comments below the bar.
options.reason: A stronger general instruction is still a general instruction: it does not define which issues count, so it cuts volume without improving precision.

options.text: Replace the confidence line with categories to report, such as bugs and security flaws, and categories to skip, such as minor style.
options.reason: Specific categorical criteria tell Claude which issues to report and which to skip, which improves precision where confidence-based instructions failed.

options.text: Ask Claude to attach a numeric confidence score to each finding, and post to the pull request only the findings scored above 0.9.
options.reason: This still relies on confidence-based filtering, which the guide says to replace with specific criteria for what to report and what to skip.

options.text: Keep the confidence line and add the missed null-pointer bugs as few-shot examples, so that Claude learns to report them again.
options.reason: It keeps the general confidence instruction and never defines style as a category to skip, so the style false positives remain.
